headline: Town boards split sharply on Special Town Meeting spending articles as Neary School narrowed building options and Costco hearings began.
synopsis: In September, Southborough boards positioned themselves for the October Special Town Meeting, revealing stark divides between town committees over spending. The Select Board and Community Preservation Committee endorsed $433,546 in CPA funds for golf course irrigation, but the Advisory Committee unanimously rejected it and joined the Select Board in opposing additional funds for the Peninsula Trail footbridge. Meanwhile, the Elementary School Building Committee eliminated an exterior gym addition for Neary Elementary School, narrowing focus to renovation plans and a $15 million baseline repair scope. The Planning Board opened public hearings on Costco's proposed 167,000-square-foot retail warehouse and 15-pump gas station, confronting questions over traffic and loading dock noise. Across town departments, officials began preparing dual FY28 budget scenarios in anticipation of a potential operational tax override in the spring.

top_items.title: Neary School Building Committee narrows design options
top_items.why: The committee voted to eliminate Option 4 and focus consultants on Option 1, Option 3, and a $15 million baseline repair scope.
top_items.body: With initial cost projections ranging between $24.4 million and $49.2 million, the Elementary School Building Committee voted 3-1 to drop Option 4 (an exterior gym addition) due to difficult soil conditions and site costs. The committee directed architects to focus on Option 1, Option 3 (enclosing the courtyard for a 400-seat gym), and a scoped $15 million baseline repair option. Educators and staff expressed strong support for Option 3, which satisfies district programming needs while preserving existing athletic fields.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee and Select Board split on golf irrigation funding
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 0-7 against recommending $433,546 in CPA funds for golf irrigation, while the Select Board voted 5-0 in favor.
top_items.body: Bids to replace the failing irrigation system at the Southborough Golf Club came in well above original estimates, driving total project costs to nearly $1.09 million. The proposal seeks $433,546 from the Community Preservation Act alongside $100,000 from the Golf Course Revolving Fund. The Advisory Committee strongly opposed the measure, arguing that the self-sustaining course should rely on user fees rather than town CPA funds, while the Select Board and CPC endorsed the funding article for Special Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail bridge funding faces united board opposition
top_items.why: Both the Select Board (1-4) and the Advisory Committee (0-7) voted against recommending $217,318 in additional CPA funding for the pedestrian footbridge.
top_items.body: The Southborough Trails Committee requested $217,318 in supplemental CPA funds to build a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian footbridge along Route 30, bringing the total project cost to $428,550 after earlier bids exceeded original estimates. Although supported 5-0 by the Community Preservation Committee, the article met stiff resistance from the Select Board and Advisory Committee over cost escalation during a constrained fiscal environment. The Trails Committee plans voter outreach and may seek to extend existing unspent funds before the deadline.

top_items.title: Planning Board opens hearing on Coslin Drive Costco proposal
top_items.why: Costco presented plans for a 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 15-pump gas station, drawing scrutiny over traffic and noise.
top_items.body: The Planning Board began reviewing major site plan and special permit applications for the 26.12-acre parcel at 21 Coslin Drive, spanning Southborough and Westborough. The project proposes a 167,000-square-foot retail building and a fueling station with 30 dispensing positions, along with stormwater wetlands and 36-foot dark-sky lighting. Board members and residents raised concerns over regional traffic congestion on Route 9, truck delivery routes, and loading dock noise impacting nearby neighborhoods.

top_items.title: Two-family zoning amendment advances to Special Town Meeting
top_items.why: The Select Board and ZBA endorsed eliminating the two-year wait for two-family conversions, while Advisory recommended disapproval.
top_items.body: Article 2 proposes removing the mandatory two-year waiting period to convert single-family homes into two-family dwellings and establishes zoning definitions to regulate new construction by special permit. The Advisory Committee voted 3-4 against recommending the measure due to concerns regarding neighborhood density, municipal services, and septic limits. The Select Board unanimously backed a revised draft after the ZBA cleaned up definitions, but the Planning Board continued its public hearing to October 17 to review potential floor amendments addressing district lot size rules.

top_items.title: Departments model dual FY28 budgets facing projected deficit
top_items.why: The Personnel Board recommended a 5% salary increase while departments were directed to prepare both level-service and flat budgets.
top_items.body: Facing an operating deficit projected to exceed $2 million, Southborough departments began assembling dual budget submissions for FY28 ahead of an earlier March Town Meeting. Budget A models level services including a 5% total wage increase (3% COLA plus 2% steps) recommended by the Personnel Board, anticipating a potential spring tax override. Budget B models a zero-growth freeze that would force staff reductions and line-item cuts in departments such as the Library, Health, and Conservation.

top_items.title: School committees approve $22,750 salary adjustment for superintendent
top_items.why: All four school committees voted to grant Superintendent Gregory Martineau a $22,750 market correction to his base salary.
top_items.body: Meeting jointly, the Southborough, Northborough, Regional, and Superintendency Union No. 3 committees approved a $22,750 base salary adjustment for Superintendent Gregory Martineau for 2026-2027, increasing his salary to $270,213 retroactive to July 1. Officials stated the raise will be absorbed within existing operating budgets. In the same meeting, Algonquin Regional High School administration announced it paused the planned rollout of the Doorman geofencing mobile app for student cell phone enforcement following privacy concerns.
